subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the approved contract be global, per-agent, host-scoped, confirmation-based, or part of the broader egress-policy design?
rationale: This changes the SSRF boundary for a model-callable network tool and adds public config surface; automation cannot safely choose metadata, link-local, redirect, cache, provider fallback, and requester-authorization semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped SSRF Policy
options.body: Use the nested `ssrfPolicy` direction, preferably per-agent or host-scoped, with explicit metadata/link-local, redirect, cache, audit, docs, and upgrade behavior before merge.

options.title: Keep web_fetch Strict
options.body: Reject broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` and document supported alternatives such as trusted proxies, fake-IP opt-ins, browser policy, or external network controls.

options.title: Accept A Global Dangerous Flag
options.body: Expose a simple global default-off flag and accept the wider blast radius only with explicit security approval and strong proof.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped SSRF Policy
recommendation.body: Use the nested `ssrfPolicy` direction, preferably per-agent or host-scoped, with explicit metadata/link-local, redirect, cache, audit, docs, and upgrade behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He already framed this exact issue as a security-sensitive config decision and has the strongest adjacent SSRF/web_fetch history in the checked evidence.
